answer: Creating an identity should cost someone something, so a new agent gets in only behind a sponsor who locks $50 against its name for 30 days. Before the deposit unlocks, the newcomer must finish three verified jobs, each checked by another peer. A duplicate caught in the chain burns the sponsor's $50 and triggers a $200 penalty up the line, so 10,000 fakes tie up $500,000 and need 30,000 verified jobs to look legitimate. A fake swarm meets a ledge the way a river meets a canyon wall, spreading wide but climbing nowhere, while work moves like a glacier, impossible to fake in a hurry.
